For the chosen number of days no loosening change is possible at all (higher limits, shorter windows, removing apps, turning protection off, removing the PIN, shortening the wait…). It cannot be cancelled. Emergency unlock still works, with limits on count and spacing.

With the PIN and a reason you can pause blocks for %1$d min. Set a daily limit. During commitment mode uses must be at least %2$d min apart. Everything is logged.
As a device administrator the app cannot be uninstalled directly from Settings. Deactivating needs the PIN and the waiting period. It cannot stop Safe Mode or a factory reset.
Time is counted from device uptime, not the clock, so changing the clock grants nothing. Windows follow the \"home time zone\".
Change home zone to the device zone
The home time zone will change to \"%1$s\". Because this shifts windows, it applies after %2$d min.

Himatsubushi Guard is a self-control aid. It never goes online; all records stay on the device.

- The guard (Usage access, Accessibility, the background service) can be switched off in system settings. The app detects and logs that and shows a restore screen, but cannot fully prevent it.
- Safe Mode, ADB, a factory reset and other ways of uninstalling cannot be stopped.
- It has no way to bypass limits set by someone else (a guardian, Family Link…). It cannot be used for that.

The aim is to add a small brake — a waiting period and an honest record — to impulsive moves you would regret.
This app helps you keep limits you set for yourself. To work well it needs a few special permissions. Each one is explained below.

This is a self-control aid. A determined person can still uninstall it, use Safe Mode or factory-reset. The app just adds a pause (waiting period) and an honest record first. It never uses the network; all data stays on the device.
Needed to know which app you use and for how long. Settings → Apps → Special app access → Usage access → turn this app on.
Needed to show the lock screen on top of other apps. Turn on \"Display over other apps\".
Used for the ongoing \"guarding\" notification, which also makes Android less likely to stop the app.
Exempts the app from battery optimisation so the system does not stop it. Important for the guard to keep running.

Recommended (the app works without it). Detects app switches instantly, and lets the app block Settings pages like App info and Accessibility during blocked windows. It reads screen text but never stores or sends it.\n\nOn Android 13+, for sideloaded apps the toggle may be greyed out. Open App info, tap the ⋮ menu (top right) and choose \"Allow restricted settings\", then open Accessibility again.
Optional. Makes the app harder to uninstall from Settings. It asks for no lock or wipe powers. Turning it off needs this app\'s PIN and a waiting period.
A 4–8 digit number that guards settings, emergency unlock and stopping focus. It is stored only as a salted hash.

- Waiting period: loosening changes apply only after your chosen wait (default 10 min). Tightening is instant.
- Commitment: for the chosen days no loosening is possible.
- Emergency unlock: 5 minutes with PIN and a reason, limited and always logged.
- Clock: changing the device clock does not grant time.
- Protection: during windows and commitment, pages like this app's info and Accessibility cannot be opened.
- Honesty report: a plain weekly list of anything that looks like tampering.

- Safe Mode, ADB, factory reset and other ways to uninstall cannot be stopped.\n- If Accessibility or Usage access is revoked the app detects and logs it and shows a \"restore permissions\" screen whenever you open another app, but cannot block the Home button.\n- It has no feature to evade limits set by someone else (a guardian, Family Link…).
Please grant Usage access and Display over other apps.
A permission the guard needs was turned off
This screen appears whenever you open another app until it is restored. Grant the items below in Settings.
If Accessibility is greyed out, open App info → ⋮ → \"Allow restricted settings\".
The Home button still works. The change is recorded in your honesty report.
